corrected_value.title: Product Entitativity: How the Presence of Product Replicates Increases Perceived and Actual Product Efficacy

decisions.quote:
In the seventh installment of
Data Replicada
, we report our attempt to replicate a recently published
Journal of Consumer Research
(JCR) article entitled, “Product Entitativity: How the Presence of Product Replicates Increases Perceived and Actual Product Efficacy” (
.html
).
In this paper, the authors propose that “presenting multiple product replicates as a group (vs. presenting a single item) increases product efficacy perceptions because it leads consumers to perceive products as more homogenous and unified around a shared goal” (abstract).
This JCR paper contains five studies. We chose to replicate Study 1 (N = 87) because it was the only study run on MTurk.
decisions.reason: The primary text explicitly identifies the replicated target as Study 1 of the recently published (2020) Journal of Consumer Research article entitled 'Product Entitativity: How the Presence of Product Replicates Increases Perceived and Actual Product Efficacy'. This uniquely matches the shipped original record (VanBergen, Irmak, & Sevilla, 2020, DOI 10.1093/jcr/ucaa006) as well as blind target 0, which recorded the identical title but left authors, year, and DOI empty because the hyperlink metadata was stripped in the plaintext scrape.

decisions.quote: As you can see, the original finding did not replicate. Participants did not judge Dettol to be significantly more effective after seeing an add that displayed five (vs. one) bottles of it.
decisions.reason: With the dependent target identity resolved to Study 1 of 'Product Entitativity: How the Presence of Product Replicates Increases Perceived and Actual Product Efficacy', the replicating authors state an explicit overall verdict across their three preregistered replications that the original finding did not replicate (which the original authors also acknowledge in the author feedback section). Both shipped and blind codings accurately record 'failed'.

decisions.quote: We ran three identical replications. The first two were run on MTurk using the same criteria the original authors used.
decisions.reason: The study collected new data across three independent MTurk samples using the original Qualtrics survey materials to re-test the published finding from Study 1 of the original JCR article. Both shipped and blind codings accurately classify the record type as 'replication'.
